caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 401 of 2008 with Civil Rule No. 675(FM)/2008.
lawyer:
MI Farooqi with Ruhul Quddus Advocates ------ For the Appellant. 

AKM Badrudozza Advocate ------ For the Respondent No 4. 

MAK Golam Mohiuddin Advocate ------ For the Respondent Nos. 8-11.
parties:
Dr SKM Joynul Abedin ------ Appellant
vs. 
Bangladesh & others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order plaintiff preferred the instant Appeal. A separate application for injunction was submitted by him whereupon Civil Rule No. 675 (fm)/08 was initiated and pending hearing of the rule parties were directed to maintain status quo in respect of the possession and position of the suit property pending hearing of the rule parties were directed to maintain status-quo in respect of the possession and position of the suit property. 

 3. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the appeal and the rule, in short, are that plaintiff appellant Dr. SKM Joynal Abedin instituted Title Suit No. 1605 of 2008 in the 3rd Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka against defendant respondent Nos. 1-7 Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works and its functionaries including the Chairman, National Housing Authority, Housing Bhaban, Segun Bagirha, Dhaka for a declaration that notice issued upon him on 2-3-2008 under the signature of defendant No. 6 (Deputy Director, Land), National Housing. Authority treating him as an unauthorized occupant and directing him to vacate a piece of land measuring 2.083 kathas at the suit land was illegal, null and void and not binding upon him. He also sought a decree directing the defendants to rectify the indenture of lease made on 17 June, 1991 being Deed No. 3192 in respect of Plot No. 61, Road No. 4, Block-B. Section 12, Mirpur Housing Estate as described in the schedule of the plaint. 

 4. It deserves mentioned here that during the pendency of the suit 4 other persons were added as defendant Nos. 8 to 11 on their application. With the filing of the suit plaintiff also sought for an injunction against the defendants on the allegation that Plot No. 61. Road No. 4, Block-B, of section 12 under the Mirpur Housing Estate was leased out for 99 years in favour of one Shahidul Huq and 3 others namely Md Khabir Uddin, Mr Sikandar Ali and Md Mostafa Kamal by lease a deed dated 17-6-1981. Though in the deed of lease, lease was shown to have been given of 376 Square yards, the said measurement was wrong which was later rectified enhancing the area at 533.33 Square yards and lease was granted to that effect by realizing due selami from them. While Shahidul Huq and others were in possession of Plot No. 61 they transferred the land by 4 registered deeds during the period between 1992 and 1994 in favour of the plaintiff with due approval of the National Housing Authority. Since thereafter, the plaintiff continued to possess the plot No. 61. In the month of May 2007 it transpired to him that the size of the plot was in reality 730.02 square yards in area but that wrongly it was mentioned as 533.33 square yards. In the locality the plaintiff, however, had been possessing the said extent of 730.02 square yards of land. Then he applied to the defendant Nos. 1-3 on 12-11-2007 to include the remaining portion of land in his lease deed and also rectify the same to that effect. But they did not take any step. On the contrary terming him to be an unauthorised occupant, the defendants issued notice of eviction upon him on 2-3-2008 Such notice was illegal. Under the circumstances, he instituted the suit for rectification of the deed of lease by inclusion therein remaining 196.87 square yards of land and further, as stated earlier, prayed for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from evicting him in pursuance of the notice issued by them on 2-3-2008 and 30-3-2008. 

 5. Defendant No. 3 National Housing Authority represented by its Chairman and the added defendants resisted plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction by filing separate written objections. It was contended therein that the plaintiff purchased 533.33 square yards of land out of plot No. 61 from the earlier lessees and had been possessing the same. On the other hand, 375 square yards of land contained in plot No. 62 was leased out to added defendant Momtaz Begum Azizuddin Ahmed, MM Kamaluddin and Nurunnahar on 29-2-1988 and a deed of lease was registered in their favour. Subsequently lessees Kemal Uddin, Azizuddin and Momtaz Begum appointed Shahidul Huq as their attorney to look after their affairs in respect of land of plot No. 62. It was further contended by them that there was a strip of land measuring 2.08 kathas of land lying vacant in between plot Nos. 61 and 62 lessees of plot No. 62 Nurun Nahar and Shahidul Huq Siddique applied for allotment of the said strip of land in their favour. On assessing the value of the land at double the price of the prevailing market rate, defendant No. 3 leased out the said extent of land in their favour by observing the necessary formalities. Accordingly, they also deposited a sum of Take 2,39,962 as salami. At the time of delivery of possession of the land it was found that the plaintiff raised a semi pucca structure thereon and rented out the same to garment factory. Under such circumstances, notices were issued upon the plaintiff for vacating the land. According to the objecting defendants the plaintiff had no cause of action for instituting the suit. They also prayed for rejecting the plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction. 

 6. Learned Joint District Judge by his impugned judgment and order found that the plaintiff had no occasion to claim land in plot No. 6 exceeding 533.33 square yards of land which he purchased from the earlier lessees Shahidul Huq and 3 others during the year 1992 and 1993 with the approval of the government and that he was a trespasser in respect of vacant strip of 2.08 kathas of land and rejected his prayer for temporary injunction. 

 7. As stated at the beginning, being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order plaintiff preferred instant appeal being FMA No. 401 of 2008 and also prayed for temporary injunction by a separate application which gave rise to a Civil Rule being No. 675 (fin) 2008. At the time of issuance of the rule parties were directed to maintain status quo in respect of the possession and position of the suit property. 

 8. Mr. MI Farooqui, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff appellant, has submitted before us that plot No. 61 contains a compact piece of land within the boundary mentioned therein. The site plan and the yellow cultured portion thereof showed the identity of the land delivered for physical possession. According to him there was a mutual mistake of the parties in measuring the area of land. Them was thus a good prima facie case in favour of the plaintiff appellant petitioner and balance of convenience and inconvenience was also in his favour in matter of injunction. So, he has submitted for allowing the appeal setting aside the impugned judgment and order of rejection of temporary injunction and thereby restraining the defendant respondent opposite parties from disturbing in his peaceful possession of the suit property till disposal of the suit now pending before the court below. Mr Farooqi in support of his submission has cited before as the decision in the case of Mr Delhi Gramani vs CR Ramachandran, reported in AIR 1953 (Madras) at 769-774, another decision in the case of Modern Talkies vs Chowrangee Cinema Hall, reported in 28 DLR 414 and the other decision in the case of AKM Abul Kashem vs Kartrik, Chandra Shit, reported in 7 BLC 452. 

 9. Mr AKM Badruduzza, learned Advocate representing respondent No. 4 (Opposite Party No. 4 in the rule) has fully supported the impugned judgment and order of the learned Joint District Judge rejecting plaintiff appellants prayer for temporary injunction. According to him a trespasser's possession cannot be protected. He has further drawn our attention to the counter affidavit submitted by him in Civil Rule No. 675(fm)/2008 on 12-4-2009 and also to the documents and papers submitted by him by means of a supplementary affidavit dated 11-5-2009. He has submitted that the vacant strip of 2.083 kathas of land was lawfully leased out to the lessee of plot No. 62 by observing necessary formalities under due process of law. Plaintiff having been found to be an illegal occupant of the said strip of land notice was legally issued upon him for vacating the same. By the way he has also submitted that the prayer for decree of rectification of the deed of leases by way of inclusion of the said extent of land in his favour was not at all maintainable inasmauch, as such, rectification was not sought by the earlier lessess from whom the plaintiff purchased 533.33 square yards of land. According to him the appeal will be dismissed and the rule for injunction discharged. In support of his submission he has cited a decision in the case of Abdul Mannan Fakir vs Province of East Pakistan, reported in 17 DLR 319 holding that the court should see if plaintiff has some personal interest in the matter and if so, whether such interest would suffer in the event of not issuing an order of ad interim injunction immediately. In his view personal interest does not mean interest without right. 

 11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates and have also perused the impugned judgment and order refusing plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction and also the documents submitted by way of supplementary affidavits by the appellants and the respondents. It is admitted by the parties that one Shahidul Huq Siddique and 3 others took 99 years lease of 3.75 square yards of land from plot No. 61 by a deed of lease dated 17-6-1981. Afterwards it was found that the area was wrongly mentioned as 3.75 square yards of land in place of 533.33 square yards. The deed of lease was corrected accordingly. It is admitted that the plaintiff purchased the said 533.33 square yards of land from the earlier lessees Shahidul Huq Siddique and 3 others by 4 registered deeds of purchase during 1992-1994 with the approval of the National Housing Authority. According to the plaintiff, it dawned upon him after 13 years of such purchase in the month of May 2007 that plot No. 61 actually contained 730.20 square yards of land. Then the applied to the concerned housing authority for rectification of the lease deed but instead, notices were served upon him on 2-3-2008 and 30-3-2008 for vacating the said extent of land measuring 2.083 kathas of land. 

 12. It has not been denied that one Nurunnahar and 3 others were given lease of 375 square yards of land of plot No. 62, beside plot No. 61 by a deed of lease dated 29-2-1988. The said Nurunnahar and 3 other lessees of plot No. 62 are respondent Nos. 8-11 before us. The supplementary affidavit supported by documents furnished by respondent No. 4. Chairman National Housing Authority shows that respondent Nos. 8-11 applied for allotment of the said strip of land located between plot Nos. 61 and 62 on 2-2-1997. Assistant Commissioner (Settlement) then vide his Memo No. 1334.02(1) dated 4-3-1997 directed the Executive Engineer Dhaka, Housing Settlement Division No. 1 to send a report with layout plan mentioning the area of strip of land with his opinion whether the same could be treated as an independent plot. Subsequent events show that after a thorough and lengthy process of enquiry through the hierarchy of appropriate officers of the National Housing Authority it was found that it was not proper to treat the said strip of land as an individual plot inasmuch as its length was greater than its requisite breath and was not suitable for allotment as an independent Plot So proposal was made for allotment of the said extent of land in favour of the lessees of plot No. 62 by realizing salami at double the rate of the prevailing market price of the land, which was ultimately approved in the 40th Board Meeting of the National Housing Authority on 4-10-2006. Then the strip of land was allotted in favour of respondent Nos. 8-11 vide Memo No. MP 338/78/8683 dated 5-11-2006. Supplementary counter affidavit dated 13-5-2009 supported by photocopy of two treasury chalans on behalf of respondent Nos. 8-11 shows that a sum of Taka 3,69.943 has also been realized from them. Process started for delivery of possession to them when it was found that the plaintiff occupied the said strip of land illegally. It is admitted that notices were issued upon the plaintiff to vacate the land. 

 13. Mr MI Farooqi has drawn our attention to the original layout plan of plot No. 61 and has submitted that the yellow painted area showed that the entire area of land (covering 720.30) was delivered to the lessees. We, however, find that the yellow coloured portion did not cover the entire area of plot No. 61. There was some vacant portion in the white at the right side thereof and to the left side of plot No. 62. There was hardly any occasion for the plaintiff to claim the extra area of land covering 720.30 square yards are when the original lease deed of the lessees from whom he purchased land of plot No. 61 showed that they took lease of 533.33 square yards of land. The said lessees did never come with a claim that they were entitled to possession of 720.30 square yards of land and that they ever possessed it. 

 14. Further, the original lease deed (Annexure-C) has been submitted before in by the plaintiff through supplementary affidavit dated 10-5-2009 which shows that in schedule 11 of the deed, the rent of the land was assessed and fixed in terms of per hundred square yards, Even in his plaint the plaintiff expressed willingness to pay price for the said extra strip of land in terms of measurement of the area. By no stretch of imagination it could be said that the plaintiff had any reason to claim any area in excess of 533.33 square yards of land purchased by him from the leases of plot No. 61. It has been brought to our notice by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 4 that in terms of condition No. 7 of the deed of lease the lessee was not authorized to use the land otherwise than for residential purpose. But it is found from Annexure 16 of the supplementary affidavit dated 11-5-2009 filed by the respondent No. 4 that the plaintiff submitted an application apprising the National Housing Authority that he established a diagnostic laboratory there, which was certainly contrary to the manner of use as provided in condition No. 7 of the deed of case. Nothing was even furnished by the plaintiff before the court below to show that he obtained any permission of the National Housing Authority for the purpose. 

 16. We have also carefully perused the decision cited by Mr MI Farooqi in the case of Delli Gramani vs CR Ramachandran, reported in AIR 1953 Madras 769-774. The decision related to sale of a coconut tope for the price of Rs Two lakhs. Subsequent to the execution and registration of the deed it was found that the description of the property given therein was not correct. Though in the deed it was shown that the property measured 6 cawnies 5 grounds there was a deficiency of about 21 grounds. On that count the plaintiff claimed a sum of Taka 32,500 by way of compensation on the basis of fishing price per ground. Their Lordship found that there was no occasion to allow the prayer of compensation as price was not fixed in the deed on the basis of ground and that the boundary as given in the deed would prevail. The facts and circumstances of the said case are not similar to the facts and circumstances of the instant case. In the instant case before us the sale was on the basis of square yards. The land is in the heart of the Metropolitan City meant for residential purpose. The boundary mentioned therein was simply for the purpose of location and identification of the land, not the area contained there-in. In the schedule of the original lease deed the area sold has been shown to be 533.33 square yards of land 4 deeds of sale whereby the plaintiff purchased the suit property from original lessesses show that he purchased 533.33 square yards of land, not 730 square yards. This is not an agricultural land in rural area where is a matter of established principle boundary prevails in case of dispute between area and boundary. We have no reason to hold that the same principle is equally applicable in respect of residential plot in a Metropolitan area where land was measured and its price fixed per square yard and square foot. Decision cited in the case of Modern Talkies vs Chowrangee Cinema Hall reported in 28 DLR at 414 does not appear to us to be much helpful in the instant case. The said decision showed that the dispute related to priority of right of exhibition of a specific film in different Halls of Dinajpur district town regarding which the distributor entered into oral agreements with the cinema hall owners. We have also perused the decision in the case of AKM Abul Kashem vs Kartick Chandra Shil, reported in 7 BLC 452 where protection was given to a trespasser who had at least some documents of title, however, contentious. But we do not think that same principle is applicable in our present case. The plaintiff has no document of title contentious or otherwise that he purchased 730 square yards of land exceeding 533.33 square yards from Plot No. 61. Earlier lessees from whom he purchased 533.33 square yards of land did not even claim such an inflated area of 730.20 square yards. In fact, principles of injunction have been laid down in consideration of the subject matter of the suit and the nature and extent of right involved therein. It is not everywhere the same. However, by now it has become an established principle of law that a trespasser cannot be favoured with a relief of injunction either temporary or perpetual. 

 17. In view of our findings above we hold that the learned Joint District Judge rightly refused plaintiff appellant's prayer for temporary injunction. The same does not call for any interference.
